meta.title: Use of Plant Collection Kit in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To systematically collect, press, preserve, and document wild plant specimens for pharmacognostic authentication, herbarium preparation, and crude drug source verification as per standard botanical collection protocols.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory and field collection trips for systematic collection of medicinal plant specimens for identification, voucher deposition, and teaching herbaria.
procedure: Obtain required permissions before collection — check for forest department clearances or landowner permissions as applicable.
Select healthy, mature plants showing characteristic features: leaves, flowers, fruits, and roots where possible.
Use sharp secateurs or pruning shears to make clean cuts without tearing — collect a representative branch (30–45 cm) bearing multiple leaves, buds, and flowers.
For root/underground parts: use a digging trowel; collect the minimum required while leaving enough for plant survival.
Place fresh specimens immediately in a polythene collection bag to prevent wilting.

Record field data immediately at the time of collection in the field notebook: date, location (GPS coordinates), altitude, habitat type, plant name (local/botanical), collector name, collection number.
Photograph the plant in situ: whole plant, leaves (upper and lower surface), flowers/fruits, bark, and habitat.
On return to the laboratory, remove specimens from bags and spread on clean, dry newspapers.
Remove excess soil from roots using a soft brush.
Arrange specimens on herbarium-size blotting paper (28 × 42 cm) — straighten leaves showing both surfaces; open flowers to display reproductive parts.
Fold the blotting paper around the specimen and place between several layers of newspaper.
Stack pressed specimens with additional newspaper layers and place in a plant press; tighten the press firmly.
Change blotting paper every 24 hours for the first 3–4 days.
Once dried (7–14 days), mount specimens on herbarium sheets with gum or adhesive tape.
Attach a printed herbarium label with all collection data.
Deposit authenticated voucher specimens in the institutional herbarium; record the voucher number.
Process collected material for crude drug preparation: clean, dry, and powder as per protocol.
precautions: Never collect from protected, endangered, or CITES-listed species without proper authorization.
Do not collect more plant material than required — minimize ecological impact.
Wear gloves when collecting plants with irritant latex or thorns.
Label specimens immediately at the time of collection — never rely on memory.
Photograph all specimens before pressing — fresh specimens provide better photographic quality.
Do not collect from roadside or polluted areas for chemical analysis — atmospheric deposition contaminates samples.
Handle pressed specimens with care once dry — they are extremely brittle.
Treat all specimens with pest repellent (paradichlorobenzene or thymol) before herbarium storage.
